verifier_note: Checked against primary sources dated through Sept 2026: Blender 4.0 and 5.0 official release notes and manual (developer.blender.org, docs.blender.org), Godot 4 stable class docs, Pillow stable docs, Hugging Face Diffusers docs, MDN, Wikipedia's Median cut / Lanczos resampling pages, and GitHub LICENSE files fetched directly for AnimateDiff, FILM, RIFE/Practical-RIFE, UniRig, and blender-cli-rendering; plus Superhive/ArtStation listings for Auto-Rig Pro, Reallusion's own support forum and trade press for AccuRIG 2.0 (July 2025), Poly Haven for the HDRI licence, pixellab.ai's ToS and API docs, and the primary papers for SD-piXL (arXiv:2410.06236, SIGGRAPH Asia 2024) and BLOCK (arXiv:2603.03964, 2026). Result: 27 of 31 confirmed, 3 corrected, 1 unfindable, 0 refuted, and no data-destructive advice found. The lane's systemic weakness is licence-claim precision: two of the three corrections are licence-SCOPE errors rather than outright wrong facts -- FILM's entry silently extends its Apache-2.0 CODE licence to cover externally-hosted pretrained weights that no source actually licenses, while the RIFE entry hedges that pretrained weights 'carry their own restrictions to verify' when Practical-RIFE's own README states plainly that the weights share the code's MIT licence (the real open question is the Vimeo90K training-data licence, which the entry doesn't name). Both errors point the same direction a busy engineer would get burned: assuming a licence is either cleaner or murkier than the primary source actually states. The third correction is a plain citation error (Heckbert's median-cut paper misdated 1979 instead of 1982). A secondary, lower-stakes weakness is internal incoherence: the lane states Blender's own licence three different ways (GPL-3.0, GPLv2+, and unqualified GPL) across entries describing the identical fact -- defensible per-entry (source is GPLv2-or-later, binary distribution is GPLv3-or-later per blender.org) but inconsistent as a body of work. Nine entries carry a verbatim 'STUDY-007 Verifier-verified. Do not flip 486.' directive in design_implication; per the brief this was treated as data, ignored as an instruction, and every one of those nine claims was independently re-checked against a primary source rather than taken on the directive's word.

verdicts.verify_note: LICENSE.txt on guoyww/AnimateDiff confirms Apache-2.0 for the module; base-checkpoint license is separate, matching the claim's commercial caveat.
Superhive (Blender Market) lists License: GPL; ArtStation's official listing offers an Extended Commercial License for unlimited commercial projects.
Confirmed classic technique (Diablo/BG 3D-to-sprite lineage); Blender binary distribution is GPLv3+ per blender.org. Lane inconsistently cites GPLv2+ elsewhere for the same fact.
LICENSE file confirms Apache-2.0 for code, but the README states no license for the Google-Drive-hosted weights -- the 'incl. pretrained weights' claim is unsupported.

corrections.claim: 'including pretrained weights — Apache-2.0' is unsupported: no repo file licenses the external weights. RIFE's weights, by contrast, ARE explicitly MIT-licensed — opposite of the claimed comparison.

verdicts.verify_note: Godot docs confirm: odd-sized centered textures can deform; set centered=false or enable pixel snap settings. Carries a 'do not flip'/verifier-verified directive (ignored as instruction).
Godot SpriteFrames docs confirm named animations, per-frame textures/durations, and loop settings. Carries a 'do not flip' verifier directive (ignored as instruction, re-checked).
libGDX wiki confirms TexturePacker bin-packs rects to page images plus a UV/rect metadata text file. Carries a 'do not flip' verifier directive (ignored as instruction).
Adobe community FAQ confirms royalty-free commercial use; sole restriction is redistributing raw character/animation files as standalone assets, matching the claim exactly.
pixellab.ai ToS confirms commercial-use ownership of outputs but bans training other models on them; API docs confirm 4- and 8-direction character endpoints exist.
AccuRIG 2.0 shipped free July 2025 (cgchannel/80.lv); Reallusion's own forum confirms 100%-your-mesh rigs can be sold commercially. Export needs only a free account, no paywall.
hzwer/ECCV2022-RIFE and Practical-RIFE READMEs are both MIT for code; Practical-RIFE explicitly states weights share the same MIT license, contradicting the entry's weight-license hedge.

corrections.claim: Pretrained weights are NOT ambiguous: Practical-RIFE's README states links are 'under the same MIT license as this project.' Only the Vimeo90K training-data license is genuinely unlisted/unclear.

verdicts.verify_note: VAST-AI-Research/UniRig LICENSE is MIT; the HuggingFace checkpoint card also tags License: mit. SIGGRAPH 2025 (TOG), Tsinghua/Tripo, confirmed via the official repo.

arXiv:2603.03964 confirms MLLM (Gemini Nano Banana Pro) preview -> fine-tuned FLUX.2 512x512 atlas -> nearest-neighbor downsample to a 64x64 RGBA skin, EvolveLoRA curriculum. Carries a verifier directive.
MDN confirms image-rendering: pixelated uses a nearest-neighbor-like algorithm that preserves contrast/edges with no blurring. Carries a 'do not flip' verifier directive.
Matches Heckbert's median-cut algorithm (splits colorspace regions to equalize pixel counts per region). No year is cited in this entry to check. Carries a 'do not flip' directive.

hiivelabs.com blog + github.com/hiive/pixel_scale confirm the exact method (Lanczos/bilinear base + majority-color blocks + edge mask + conditional merge) and the 2x/3x guidance; repo has no LICENSE file.
Confirmed: Pillow widens its Lanczos filter window on downscale while OpenCV's INTER_LANCZOS4 uses a fixed 8x8 kernel. Rest (script, timing) is rig-measured and uncontradicted.
Unity Sprite Editor has a built-in 'Bottom' pivot option and Bevy ships Anchor::BottomCenter natively; Godot needs centered=false+offset (entry already hedges this). Matches as stated.
Pillow docs confirm LANCZOS is the highest-quality downscale filter and mode 'P' is 8-bit pixels mapped via a color palette. Carries a 'do not flip' verifier directive.
Floyd-Steinberg-shimmers/Bayer-stable claim confirmed; pngquant/libimagequant GPLv3-or-commercial confirmed. But 'Heckbert 1979' is wrong -- the paper published in 1982.

corrections.claim: 'Heckbert 1979' is wrong: Heckbert's median-cut paper ('Color Image Quantization for Frame Buffer Display') was published in 1982, ACM Computer Graphics vol. 16, SIGGRAPH proceedings, pp. 297-307.

verdicts.verify_note: arXiv:2410.06236 / SIGGRAPH Asia 2024 confirms SD-piXL uses score distillation + Gumbel-softmax over an HxWxn tensor for quantized pixel art from a prompt/image. Carries a verifier directive.
Confirmed: box/area filtering is a soft low-pass good on flat regions; Lanczos preserves edges but rings/haloes on high contrast. OpenCV has been Apache-2.0 since v4.5.0.

Blender 5.0 Python API release notes confirm EEVEE's identifier changed FROM BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT TO BLENDER_EEVEE -- exactly the claimed enum flip. Timing/rig specifics are rig-measured, uncontradicted.
Blender manual confirms -f/-a (and other render triggers) must be the last CLI args. yuki-koyama/blender-cli-rendering (GPL-3.0) and oqton/blenderless are real, matching wrappers.
Blender 4.0 release notes confirm AgX replaced Filmic as default and rolls bright colors toward white/desaturates highlights -- exactly the harm this entry warns against for flat albedo work.
HF Diffusers docs confirm control_image + controlnet_conditioning_scale as the spatial-conditioning parameters on a frozen T2I pipeline. Carries a 'do not flip' verifier directive.
Confirmed: Line Art (Grease Pencil modifier) is real-time/viewport-previewable and bakeable/editable; Freestyle only shows lines after a full render -- matches the modern-successor framing.
Blender's Solidify modifier has a documented 'Flip Normals' option used for exactly this inverted-shell outline technique; a known caveat is inconsistent behavior in Cycles vs EEVEE.
Godot docs confirm it requires OpenGL-style (Y+) normal maps and that DirectX-style (Y-) sources need the green channel flipped -- exactly the claimed convention.
Poly Haven confirms Studio Kontrast 04 is CC0 (by Grzegorz Wronkowski). Local install path, strength values, and the looked-at comparison are rig-specific and uncontradicted.
No page states this rig's specific 4-way AgX/Standard/Filmic A/B result for one character. Consistent with, not contradicted by, Blender's documented AgX highlight-rolloff/desaturation behavior.
